headline: Credential thieves close the gap to real-time account takeover by poisoning hotel Wi-Fi and insurance logins, as Cl0p extorts exposed PTC Windchill systems and physical wrench attacks on crypto holders climb.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers are shrinking the window between capturing a login and abusing it, hijacking hotel Wi-Fi DNS to feed guests fake Microsoft 365 pages and relaying insurance customers' credentials the moment they type them.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Hotel Wi-Fi DNS Hijacking Steals Microsoft 365 Logins

emerging_trends.text: AI coding assistants have become a soft target, tricked into recommending hallucinated package, repository, and domain names that attackers pre-register to slip malicious code into build pipelines.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Coding Agents Trust Hallucinated Packages

emerging_trends.text: Cybercrime keeps bleeding into the physical world, as researchers track a rise in wrench attacks—home invasions and kidnappings—aimed at forcing cryptocurrency holders to hand over their keys.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Wrench Attacks on Cryptocurrency Holders Rise

topics.title: Rockwell and Siemens Patch Industrial Control Flaws
topics.latest_developments: Rockwell Automation patched code-execution vulnerabilities in its Arena discrete-event simulation software, and SecurityWeek flagged fresh flaws in Siemens ROX II industrial switches, both exposing industrial operators to remote compromise.
topics.summary: Manufacturers running Rockwell Arena simulation software or Siemens ROX II switches face attacker code execution on engineering and network gear; apply the vendor updates and segment industrial control networks from corporate access.

sources.title: Rockwell Patches Code Execution Flaws in Arena Simulation Software
In Other News: Dolphin X AI-Powered Malware, Car Anti-Theft Device Hack, 400 Linux Kernel Flaws

topics.title: Cl0p Details Windchill and FlexPLM Extortion Chain
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News laid out the exploitation chain today: Cl0p affiliates pair a pre-authentication information-disclosure flaw in the FlexPLM WSDL endpoint with a server-side bug in the Windchill login servlet to run code without authentication and steal data for extortion.
topics.summary: The Cl0p gang, also tracked as Chubby Scorpius, FIN11, Graceful Spider, and Lace Tempest, is raiding internet-exposed PTC Windchill and FlexPLM product-lifecycle-management servers; operators should pull these instances off the public internet and apply PTC fixes.

sources.title: Cl0p Affiliates Target Internet-Exposed PTC Windchill and FlexPLM with Unauthenticated RCE

topics.title: Insurance Phishing Turns Into Real-Time Account Hijacking
topics.latest_developments: CTM360 disclosed that insurance-focused phishing has shifted from harvesting credentials for later use to hijacking accounts in real time, relaying each username and password the instant a victim submits it.
topics.summary: Adversary-in-the-middle phishing kits capture and replay insurance and financial customers' logins immediately, defeating one-time codes; defenders need phishing-resistant authentication and rapid session monitoring.

sources.title: CTM360 Research Reveals How Insurance Phishing Has Evolved Into Real-Time Account Hijacking

topics.title: Hotel Wi-Fi DNS Hijacking Steals Microsoft 365 Logins
topics.latest_developments: Hackers are changing DNS settings on Wi-Fi equipment at hotels and conference centers to route guests to counterfeit Microsoft 365 login pages that harvest credentials, BleepingComputer reported July 24, 2026.
topics.summary: Traveling employees who join a compromised hotel or venue network land on spoofed sign-in pages that capture usernames and passwords; guard against it with a corporate VPN, strict URL checks, and phishing-resistant multifactor authentication.

sources.title: Hackers hijack hotel Wi-Fi DNS to steal Microsoft 365 accounts

topics.title: Wrench Attacks on Cryptocurrency Holders Rise
topics.latest_developments: The Record reported that researchers now count more wrench attacks than ever—home invasions and kidnappings that strong-arm cryptocurrency holders into surrendering their funds.
topics.summary: Criminals increasingly bypass digital defenses and physically coerce known crypto holders into transferring assets; holders should limit public disclosure of their holdings and harden home and travel security.

sources.title: 'Wrench' attacks against crypto holders appear to be on the rise

topics.title: AI Coding Agents Trust Hallucinated Packages
topics.latest_developments: ActiveState argued that slopsquatting, phantom domains, and HalluSquatting all exploit one late-binding weakness—AI coding agents trusting invented package, repository, and domain names—and pushed pre-fetch verification to stop the malicious code before it reaches the pipeline.
topics.summary: Attackers pre-register the package, repo, and domain names that AI assistants hallucinate, so an agent's recommendation pulls hostile dependencies into builds; teams should verify names before fetch and enforce governed dependency management.

sources.title: Slopsquatting, Phantom Domains, and HalluSquatting Are the Same AI Attack

business_politics.title: U.S. Pauses Iran Strikes as Oman Brokers Hormuz Deal
business_politics.latest_developments: The United States halted its air campaign, and neither side attacked for a second straight night while Oman pursued a Strait of Hormuz transit deal.
business_politics.summary: The United States paused its two-week bombing of Iran, and neither combatant launched attacks for a second consecutive night as Omani mediators worked to reopen safe transit through the Strait of Hormuz, opening a possible off-ramp from a war that had driven oil prices higher.

sources.title: US pauses Iran strikes as Oman pursues Hormuz transit deal

business.title: Little Debbie Driver Charged in Snack Fraud
business.latest_developments: Pennsylvania authorities charged the driver, alleging he diverted product to flea markets and filed fake invoices to cover it.
business.summary: A delivery driver who supplied Little Debbie snack cakes to stores across Pennsylvania faces charges for selling the product at flea markets for cash and submitting falsified invoices, KDKA reported.

sources.title: Little Debbie snack delivery driver charged in fraud scheme

around_town.title: Pennsylvania Budget Relaxed School Lead Rules
around_town.latest_developments: A Spotlight PA investigation found the new state budget quietly loosened the standards schools must meet to report lead in drinking water.
around_town.summary: A provision in Pennsylvania's newly enacted state budget relaxed the reporting standards schools must follow for lead in drinking water, and Spotlight PA reporters concluded the underlying law's problems run deeper than the change, TribLive reported.

sources.title: Pa. budget quietly relaxed lead reporting standards for schools. Issues with law go much deeper.

around_town.title: Wildfire Smoke and Storms Over Pittsburgh
around_town.latest_developments: A wildfire-smoke plume settled over the region Sunday, July 26, as scattered afternoon thunderstorms returned to the forecast.
around_town.summary: Wildfire smoke drifted into the Pittsburgh area Sunday, July 26, though the plume sat roughly 7,000 feet up and spared surface air quality, while scattered thunderstorms threatened after 2 p.m. under highs in the low 80s, KDKA reported.

sources.title: Wildfire smoke rolls into Pittsburgh area today as scattered storm chances loom

around_town.title: Franklin Regional Grad Earns Tony Nomination
around_town.latest_developments: Ryan Park, a Franklin Regional graduate, earned a Tony Award nomination for his costume work.
around_town.summary: Ryan Park, a Franklin Regional Senior High School graduate from Westmoreland County who gravitated to backstage theater work as a student, earned a Tony Award nomination for costume design on 'Lost Boys,' TribLive reported.

sources.title: Franklin Regional grad earns Tony Award nomination for 'Lost Boys' costumes

around_teams.title: Pirates Sign First-Rounder Derek Curiel
around_teams.latest_developments: The Pirates officially signed 2026 first-round pick Derek Curiel, reportedly for a $6.2 million bonus.
around_teams.summary: The Pittsburgh Pirates signed LSU outfielder Derek Curiel, their 2026 first-round draft pick, to a reported $6.2 million bonus, the Post-Gazette reported, adding the club's top pick to the farm system.

sources.title: Pirates officially sign first-round draft pick Derek Curiel

around_teams.title: Revisiting the Jerry Meals Call
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette revisited the infamous Jerry Meals safe call 15 years to the day after it happened.
around_teams.summary: On July 26, 2011, umpire Jerry Meals ruled Atlanta's Julio Lugo safe at the plate in the 19th inning, handing the Braves a 4-3 win over the Pirates, and the Post-Gazette gathered Greg Brown, Michael McKenry, and others to relive one of the most infamous calls in franchise history.

sources.title: 'Jerry Meals called him safe!': Looking back at one of the most infamous and impactful calls in Pirates history

team_usa.title: Flavor Flav Fetes Team USA's Women Olympians
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN detailed a four-day Las Vegas celebration rapper Flavor Flav staged for United States women Olympians.
team_usa.summary: Rapper Flavor Flav hosted 'She Weekend,' a four-day Las Vegas celebration honoring Team USA's women Olympians, an event ESPN reported left the athletes feeling seen, celebrated, and connected.

sources.title: What happens when Flavor Flav throws a party for women Olympians?
